text: Section 5(3)(i) of the Federal Law on Assemblies, Meetings, Demonstrations, Marches and Picketing (no. 54-FZ of 18 August 2004, the Assemblies Act) provides that the organiser of a public event has the right to hold meetings, demonstrations, marches and pickets at the venues and time specified in the notice on holding the public event or as altered by agreement with the executive authority of the subject of the Russian Federation or the municipal body.
section_path: THE FACTS

text: Section 5(3)(v) of the Assemblies Act provides that the organiser of a public event has the right, in holding assemblies, meetings, demonstrations and marches, to use sound-amplifying technical devices with a level of sound corresponding to the standards and norms established in the Russian Federation.
section_path: THE FACTS
II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW

text: Section 5(4)(i) of the Assemblies Act provides that the organiser of the public event must submit to the executive authority of the subject of the Russian Federation or the municipal body a notice on holding the public event in accordance with the procedure prescribed by section 7 of the Assemblies Act.
section_path: THE FACTS
II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW

text: Section 5(4)(ii) of the Assemblies Act provides that the organiser of the public event must, no later than three days prior to the holding of the public event, notify in writing the executive authority of the subject of the Russian Federation or the municipal body of the acceptance or non-acceptance of its proposal to alter the venue and/or time of the public event as specified in the notice of the event.
section_path: THE FACTS
II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW

text: Section 5(4)(iii) of the Assemblies Act provides that the organiser of the public event must ensure compliance with the conditions for holding the public event as specified in the notice of the event or with any conditions that have been altered as a result of an agreement reached with the executive authority of the subject of the Russian Federation or the municipal body.
section_path: THE FACTS
II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW

text: Section 5(4)(iv) of the Assemblies Act provides that the organiser of the public event must require the participants in the public event to observe public order and comply with the conditions for holding the public event, and that persons who fail to comply with the lawful requirements of the organiser may be expelled from the venue.
section_path: THE FACTS
II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW

text: Section 5(4)(v) of the Assemblies Act provides that the organiser of the public event must ensure, within their competence, public order and the safety of citizens when holding the public event and, in instances specified by the Assemblies Act, perform this obligation jointly with the authorised representative of the executive authority of the subject of the Russian Federation or the municipal body and the authorised representative of the Ministry of the Interior.
section_path: THE FACTS
II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW

text: Section 5(5) of the Assemblies Act provides that the organiser of the public event shall have no right to hold it if the notice on holding the public event has not been submitted in due time or no agreement has been reached with the executive authority of the subject of the Russian Federation or the municipal body on their reasoned proposal as to the alteration of the venue and/or time of the public event.

text: Section 8 of the Assemblies Act provides that a public event may be held at any venue suitable for holding the event if its conduct does not create a threat of the collapse of buildings or structures or other threats to the safety of the participants in the public event.

text: Section 8 of the Assemblies Act provides that conditions governing bans or restrictions on holding a public event at particular venues may be specified by federal laws.

text: Section 12(1)(ii) of the Assemblies Act provides that the executive authority of the subject of the Russian Federation or the municipal body, upon receiving notice of the public event, must inform the organiser of the public event, within three days of receipt of the notice, of a reasoned proposal to alter the venue and/or time of the public event, as well as of any proposal for the organiser to bring the aims, form or other conditions for holding the event into line with the requirements of the Assemblies Act.
